text:
maria.g: Heads-up, onboarding hiccup with a HF model that uses trust_remote_code and a custom attention module. conversion failed at final validation.
hao: which model? a HF hub name?
maria.g: local checkout of `chaos-labs/chaos-7b-custom-attn` — it defines a custom config class and adds special tokens in `__init__`. I ran the redwood onboarder: 
```
python -m redwood.onboard --hf-path ./chaos-7b-custom-attn --out /tmp/redwood/chaos-7b --trust-remote-code
```
and got an embedding size mismatch during the sanity-check step.
sam.k: paste the traceback?
maria.g: here it is: 
```
RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (50257) must match the size of tensor b (50258) at /opt/conda/.../aten/src/TH/generic/THTensorMath.c:xxx
During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:
ValueError: mismatch between `config.vocab_size=50258` and tokenizer vocab (50257)
```
olivia: classic. model code is adding an extra special token at tokenizer init but not bumping `vocab_size` in config.json. HF `trust_remote_code` loaders sometimes mutate tokenizer and model in inconsistent order.
hao: did the onboarder attempt `auto_map`? that can create `AutoModelForCausalLM` that expects config.vocab_size to match embeddings.
maria.g: yes, onboarder prints `using auto_map: {"AutoModel": "custom_attn.CustomModel"}` during load. I tried passing `--force-tokenizer-sync` and still failed.
sam.k: two immediate workarounds: 1) patch config.json to match tokenizer length, or 2) edit the model code to call `tokenizer.add_special_tokens` before model.load_state_dict so config and embeddings align. Both are hacks.
maria.g: patched config.json locally to 50257 and reran; conversion completed, but quant evals look suspicious. 4-bit quantized variant shows weird degredation on our small eval set (QA F1 drop ~6 points).
olivia: did you use quantization aware config mapping? sometimes custom attention kernels are not supported by the quant runtime, fallback to slower kernels or precision mismatch causing quality regression.
hao: share the eval snippet and quant params pls.
maria.g: eval command: 
```
redwood-eval --model /tmp/redwood/chaos-7b-q4 --task squad --batch 8 --max-len 512
```
Quant params: `--quant 4 --group-size 128 --qtype nf4`
Result: baseline float32: F1 81.2, q4: F1 75.0, latency improved ~2.2x but hallucination spikes on long contexts.
sam.k: sounds like KV cache or custom attn not using the quantized kernels properly. Also check that the model's forward signature hasn't been wrapped by the custom class to do nonce ops that break int8/4 inference.
maria.g: agreed. I tried forcing `--disable-quant-optimizations` and then q4 result improved to F1 78.9 (still below baseline).
olivia: for onboarding, we should: 1) detect tokenizer/model vocabulary mutation (emit warning and auto-fix by bumping config.vocab_size or exporting a patched tokenizer.json), 2) add a check for `trust_remote_code` models to run a small forward pass and validate embedding dims before committing, 3) document quant runtime caveats for custom attention modules.
hao: +1 on runtime forward check. we can run `tokenizer_len = len(tokenizer)` and compare to `config.vocab_size` and `model.get_input_embeddings().weight.size(0)` early. auto-fix option should create `conversion_report.json` and back up originals.
maria.g: I'll open a PR with a failing test case (pack the HF repo minimal), and include repro steps and the patched-config fallback.
ci-bot: build queued: redwood/onboarder#4527, test: onboarder::trustrc-tokenizer-fix (expected flaky)
sam.k: thanks. one more note: if we auto-patch config.json, also set `model.tie_word_embeddings` flags appropriately — otherwise embedding tie ops can still blow up.
maria.g: good call. also planning to add an eval sanity job post-conversion that runs a couple of prompts to detect hallucinations/regressions early.
olivia: awesome. thanks for catching this before we onboard more trust_remote_code models. :raised_hands:
